text:
alex: Heads-up: noticed canary exposure skew for customer accounts on dedicated quotas — a few large orgs are eating most of the canary impressions. Anyone seen this?
mica: Yep. Dashboard shows top 10 orgs getting ~70% of impressions for the new decoder canary.
sam: Can you paste the routing pipeline? I thought canary sampling was done before quota checks.
alex: Current flow is: route -> sample -> assign -> quota_check. But quota_check short-circuits and falls back to the stable model. So if a big org keeps passing sampling and then later hits quota we end up counting weirdness.
alex: ```
# simplified pseudo
request -> matcher -> if random() < canary_weight: send_to_canary else send_to_stable
then: quota_check(canary) -> if fail: send_to_stable (and don't count as canary impression)
```
lina: That explains it. Effective exposure per org != global weight. Burstier tenants will distort the sample.
sam: Options: 1) quota_first (check quota before sampling) 2) per-org canary caps 3) global token-bucket for canary impressions. Each has tradeoffs.
hassan: Per-org caps are fairest but stateful. Could approximate with sharded counters (consistent-hash) to avoid global sync, but adds complexity.
mica: Product wants the console to show "effective exposure" per-org + "predicted remaining impressions" for canaries. That would make bias visible.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary config v2.3 rolled to prod on eng-platform at 1799994300. No errors.
alex: perfect timing 😂 — that deploy bumped canary weight which may have amplified this.
sam: I can prototype telemetry: canary_attempts{org,canary} and canary_confirmed{org,canary}. Then compute confirmation_rate = confirmed/attempts and surface distribution.
lina: UX idea: in Rollouts show expected_exposure = global_weight * total_attempts and actual_exposure per-org. Add a warning if |actual-expected|/expected > 30%.
alex: Implementation thoughts: sampling before quota gives fairness of exposure but risks more client-facing quota rejections later. Quota-first prevents rejections but biases exposure.
sam: How about hybrid: sample -> fast_reserve_token(global_bucket) -> if reserve_ok proceed to canary path; on final quota check confirm and decrement reserved token. If confirm fails we mark as failure but we didn't overcount.
hassan: Short TTL reservations, yes. We already use sub-second ephemeral locks in runtime for KV cache entries; reuse patterns there. Need to handle leak on host crash.
mica: For telemetry store both reserved and confirmed counts. Dashboard can show reserved vs confirmed as two bars. Designers want per-org drilldown.
lina: I'll mock a small widget: per-org sparkline + reserved/confirmed numbers + a red flag for skew. Will sync with PM.
alex: Next steps: Sam prototypes metrics + reserve-token POC. Lina to mock console widget. Mica to draft RFC on quota-before-vs-after tradeoffs. I'll run audit to list top 20 orgs by skew.
sam: tagging infra as well — might need a tiny in-memory shard for token buckets per region.
mica: Sounds good. @lina can you sync with design on Monday? :thumbsup:
lina: Yep, will put a quick Figma by EOD Mon.
incident-bot: Created ticket CAN-2393 to track canary exposure bias and assigned to eng-platform.
alex: Thanks all. If anyone sees a spike or customer complaint, ping me and I'll post updates here.
